_about: #209 review: advance widths (em) of every character the studio charts print (ASCII, the minus, middle dot, ellipsis, sub- and superscript digits and a few symbols), and the tallest glyph box above and below the baseline (em): `ascent`/`descent` for value labels (digits, separators, signs, %), `textAscent`/`textDescent` for any text (letters too: f, g, j). For the eight Design Studio faces (src/reporting/studio/render/fonts.ts), regular (400) and bold (700). Measured in Chromium 1194 from the @fontsource Latin WOFF2 files the studio serves (src/reporting/studio/fonts/files.ts): canvas measureText at 100px and SVG text with the .ds-doc CSS (lining-nums), the larger of the two; DM Serif Display has no 700 file, so its bold row is the 400 file. A character a face lacks comes from its fallback (Noto Sans, then the generic family). ci/unit/ds-209-layout.test.cjs checks that the renderer's textWidth (charts/metrics.ts), labelWidth and labelBox are never smaller than any of these. #209 round 4: `top` and `bottom` (em) are each character's ink above and below the alphabetic baseline (canvas actualBoundingBoxAscent/Descent, lining figures), and `middleShift` (em) how far dominant-baseline "middle" puts the baseline under y (SVG getBBox with and without it), for charts/metrics.ts inkExtent.
